spark.summary: A Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) is a machine-readable inventory (SPDX or CycloneDX) of every direct and transitive package, OS layer, and binary inside a build artifact. Paired with cryptographic attestations (Cosign/Sigstore) and VEX advisories, it lets teams answer 'Are we exposed to CVE-X?' in seconds rather than days.
spark.keyTakeaway: Generate CycloneDX or SPDX SBOMs inside your CI build, sign them with Sigstore Cosign alongside the container digest, and filter noise with VEX before blocking deploys.

concept.whyItMatters: Modern applications pull 80–90% of their code from open-source dependencies, often 5–10 transitive levels deep. When a zero-day like Log4Shell (`CVE-2021-44228`) or XZ Utils (`CVE-2024-3094`) drops, teams without an indexed SBOM waste days cloning repos and grepping lockfiles while attackers scan exposed endpoints in minutes.
whenToUse: Containerized and cloud-native services shipping to production where fast blast-radius queries across hundreds of microservices are critical.
Enterprise B2B software, FedRAMP, or US Executive Order 14028 compliance where customers demand verifiable SPDX/CycloneDX manifests per release.
CI/CD pipelines enforcing policy gates (OPA/Kyverno) to block unapproved licenses (AGPL) or critical reachable CVEs before admission.
whenNotToUse: Throwaway prototypes, internal hackathons, or ephemeral scripts with no external distribution or production data access.
Treating raw SBOM generation as a standalone security control—an SBOM without vulnerability matching (Grype/Trivy) and signature verification is just a static JSON file.
Scanning source repos only while ignoring OS base-image packages (`glibc`, `openssl`, `curl`) that enter during `docker build`.
keyPoints: Choose **CycloneDX** (OWASP, security/VEX-first, lighter JSON) or **SPDX** (Linux Foundation / ISO 5962, license/compliance-first)—both are supported by Syft, Trivy, and Dependency-Track.
Generate SBOMs against the **final built artifact** (OCI image digest `sha256:...` or compiled binary), not just `package.json` or `pom.xml`, so OS packages and vendored C libraries are captured.
Attach and sign SBOMs as OCI referrers using **Sigstore Cosign** (`cosign attach sbom` + `cosign sign`) so consumers can verify the inventory came from your trusted CI runner.
Use **VEX (Vulnerability Exploitability eXchange)** or reachability analysis to suppress false positives where a vulnerable function is never compiled or called.
Ingest all release SBOMs into a central graph store (OWASP Dependency-Track, Guac) to enable instant reverse-lookup: `package:purl -> affected services`.

examples.title: Zero-Day Triage in 90 Seconds Using Dependency-Track & CycloneDX
examples.scenario: A critical RCE vulnerability is disclosed in `org.apache.commons:commons-text:1.9`. The platform team manages 140 Java and Python microservices deployed across 3 EKS clusters.
examples.outcome: Querying `pkg:maven/org.apache.commons/commons-text@1.9` in OWASP Dependency-Track returns the exact 11 affected image digests and owning teams in 90 seconds, rather than running 140 CI rebuilds.

examples.title: Eliminating 78% of Base-Image Alert Noise with OpenVEX
examples.scenario: Trivy flags 42 High/Critical CVEs in a Distroless/Debian container image, blocking a production release even though 33 CVEs reside in unused CLI utilities or unreached code paths.
examples.outcome: The security team publishes a signed OpenVEX document marking those 33 CVEs `not_affected` (`vulnerable_code_not_in_execute_path`), allowing CI policy gates to stay strict on the remaining 9 real risks.

tradeOffs.pro: Build-time generators (Maven/Gradle CycloneDX plugins) see exact resolved scopes (`compile` vs. `test`) and avoid false positives on dev dependencies.
tradeOffs.con: Post-build image scanners (Syft, Trivy) capture OS packages (`apt`/`apk`) and native binaries that language plugins miss.

tradeOffs.factor: Strict CI Blocking vs. Advisory Reporting
tradeOffs.pro: Failing builds on `CRITICAL` CVEs prevents known-exploitable code from ever reaching registries.
tradeOffs.con: Zero-day disclosures with no upstream patch yet can freeze hotfix deploys unless VEX waivers or grace windows exist.

tradeOffs.pro: SPDX is an ISO/IEC 5962 standard favored by legal/licensing teams and government procurement.
tradeOffs.con: CycloneDX offers native support for VEX, SaaSBOM, and ML-BOMs with simpler schema ergonomics for AppSec tooling.

failureModes.name: Stale SBOM Drift After Base Image Rebuild
failureModes.description: A team generates an SBOM once from source lockfiles, but later rebuilds the Docker image with `FROM python:3.12-slim` pulling newer vulnerable `libssl` packages, leaving the stored SBOM out of sync.
failureModes.mitigation: Bind SBOM generation to the immutable OCI image digest (`sha256:...`) inside the final release job and reject images without matching digest attestations.

failureModes.name: Missing Transitive or Vendored Dependencies
failureModes.description: Go binaries compiled with `CGO_ENABLED=1` or Python wheels bundling `.so` C extensions hide native C/C++ libraries from naive lockfile parsers.
failureModes.mitigation: Use ELF/Mach-O/PE binary inspection (Syft/Trivy binary catalogers) and compile Go with `-buildvcs=true` so `debug.BuildInfo` embeds module hashes.

failureModes.name: Unsigned SBOMs Vulnerable to Tampering
failureModes.description: An attacker who compromises an artifact registry replaces the plain JSON SBOM file to hide a backdoored dependency.
failureModes.mitigation: Sign the SBOM as an in-toto attestation using `cosign attest --predicate sbom.cdx.json --type cyclonedx` and verify signatures in Kubernetes via Kyverno.

failureModes.name: Alert Fatigue from Unreachable CVEs
failureModes.description: Raw SBOM matching floods Slack/Jira with 500+ CVEs per week, mostly in `test` scopes or uncalled functions, causing engineers to ignore all alerts.
failureModes.mitigation: Exclude `test`/`dev` scopes during SBOM generation, prioritize via EPSS (>0.1) + CISA KEV, and layer OpenVEX/reachability filtering.

commonMistakes: Generating an SBOM from `requirements.txt` without pinned hashes (`pip freeze`) or lockfiles, missing transitive dependency versions.
Storing SBOM JSONs as ephemeral CI build logs instead of attaching them to OCI registries or ingesting them into Dependency-Track/Guac.
Including `devDependencies` (`jest`, `pytest`, `eslint`) in production SBOMs, inflating CVE counts by 3–5x.
Ignoring Package URL (`purl`) standardization (`pkg:pypi/requests@2.32.3`), breaking automated correlation across scanners.
Treating SBOM compliance as a one-time PDF export rather than continuous monitoring as new CVEs are published daily.

sections.content:
## The idea

A Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) is the software equivalent of a food nutrition label: a standardized, machine-readable graph of every component, version, Package URL (`purl`), license, and cryptographic hash inside a deliverable. The two dominant formats are **SPDX** (ISO/IEC 5962, strong on licensing and file-level provenance) and **CycloneDX** (OWASP, designed for security, services, and VEX).

An SBOM alone only answers *what* is inside a build. Its operational power comes from pairing it with **SLSA provenance** (proving *how* and *where* it was built), **Sigstore Cosign** signatures (proving *integrity* against tampering), and **VEX** (proving *exploitability* so teams fix real risks instead of chasing phantom CVEs).

## Concrete walkthrough

Here is how a hardened GitHub Actions pipeline produces and enforces an SBOM for a Go/Python microservice:

1. **Build Immutable Artifact**: `docker buildx build --push` produces `ghcr.io/acme/billing@sha256:8f91...` from pinned lockfiles (`poetry.lock` / `go.sum`).
2. **Generate SBOM**: `syft ghcr.io/acme/billing@sha256:8f91... -o cyclonedx-json=sbom.cdx.json` catalogs both OS `apk`/`dpkg` layers and language packages with standardized `purl`s.
3. **Attest & Sign (Keyless OIDC)**: `cosign attest --predicate sbom.cdx.json --type cyclonedx ghcr.io/acme/billing@sha256:8f91...` mints an ephemeral Fulcio certificate tied to the GitHub OIDC token, logs the signature in Rekor, and pushes the signed attestation as an OCI referrer.
4. **Ingest & Match**: CI uploads `sbom.cdx.json` to **OWASP Dependency-Track** and runs `grype sbom:sbom.cdx.json --vex openvex.json --fail-on critical`.
5. **Admission Gate**: Before Kubernetes schedules the pod, **Kyverno** verifies the Cosign attestation signature against the trusted GitHub Actions OIDC issuer and confirms no unwaived `CRITICAL` KEV vulnerabilities exist.

sections.content:
## SPDX, CycloneDX & Package URLs (purls)

Both NTIA-minimum-element formats share the same core goal—identifying supplier, component name, version, unique identifier, dependency relationship, author, and timestamp—but optimize for different workflows. **Package URL (`purl`)** acts as the universal primary key across both: `pkg:npm/%40babel/core@7.24.0` or `pkg:deb/debian/openssl@3.0.11-1~deb12u2?arch=amd64`.

Without standardized `purl`s and CPEs, vulnerability databases (OSV, NVD, GitHub Advisory Database) cannot reliably join an SBOM entry to a CVE. Always prefer tools that emit `purl` + `sha256` hashes for every component rather than fuzzy name/version strings.

## SBOM & supply-chain tooling comparison

| Tool | Role | Supported Formats | Key Strength | Limitation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Anchore Syft** | SBOM Generator | CycloneDX, SPDX, Syft JSON | Deep OS + language + binary cataloging | Does not scan for CVEs itself (pair with Grype) |
| **Aqua Trivy** | All-in-One Scanner | CycloneDX, SPDX | Single binary for SBOM + CVE + IaC + VEX | Less granular language-build context than native plugins |
| **OWASP Dependency-Track** | SBOM Platform | CycloneDX (native), SPDX | Central portfolio graph, VEX, policy engine | Requires PostgreSQL + JVM ops overhead |
| **Sigstore Cosign** | Signing & Attestation | in-toto / OCI Referrers | Keyless OIDC signing + Rekor transparency log | Requires OCI-compliant registry (GHCR, ECR, GAR) |

## Failure modes

**1. Language-Specific Blind Spots**: Running `syft` on a stripped static C++ binary yields zero package metadata unless debug symbols or build-time Conan/vcpkg manifests are included. For C/C++/Rust, generate the SBOM during the build step (`cargo-cyclonedx`) and merge it with the container-layer SBOM.

**2. NVD CPE Matching False Positives**: Naive NVD lookups match `cpe:2.3:a:vendor:product:*` loosely, flagging irrelevant CVEs. Prefer OSV-backed matchers (Grype, `osv-scanner`) that match exact `purl`s and commit ranges.

**3. Unbounded SBOM Size in Monorepos**: A single multi-stage image with leftover build caches can produce a 40 MB JSON SBOM, timing out registry pushes. Use multi-stage builds (`FROM scratch` or Distroless) so runtime images contain only production artifacts.

sections.eyebrow: 06 / Scaling triage with VEX and SLSA provenance
sections.content:
## Scaling triage with VEX and SLSA provenance

At >50 services, raw SBOM scanning creates unsustainable toil. Combining **EPSS** (Exploit Prediction Scoring System) with **OpenVEX** solves this: prioritize patching CVEs with `EPSS > 0.1` or listed in **CISA KEV**, and issue signed VEX statements (`status: not_affected`, `justification: vulnerable_code_not_present`) for false positives so they stay suppressed across future scans.

Simultaneously, pair your CycloneDX/SPDX SBOM with **SLSA Build Level 2/3 provenance** (`actions/attest-build-provenance`). While the SBOM lists *what* is in the box, SLSA provenance cryptographically proves *which* Git commit and *which* isolated CI runner produced it—preventing a compromised developer laptop from pushing a malicious image with a forged SBOM.

## Practical checklist

- [ ] Pin all transitive dependencies with lockfiles (`package-lock.json`, `poetry.lock`, `go.sum`, `Cargo.lock`) and verify hashes in CI.
- [ ] Generate CycloneDX or SPDX SBOMs against the final built OCI image digest (`sha256:...`), not just source directories.
- [ ] Strip `dev`/`test` dependencies and build-time toolchains via multi-stage Dockerfiles before SBOM generation.
- [ ] Sign and attach SBOMs as in-toto attestations using `cosign attest` with keyless OIDC.
- [ ] Ingest all release SBOMs into a central store (Dependency-Track) to enable sub-minute zero-day impact queries.
- [ ] Adopt OpenVEX and EPSS/CISA KEV thresholds so CI gates block real exploitable risks without stalling on unreachable CVEs.

interviewProblems.title: Supply Chain Security & SBOMs
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: Design a production system that depends on Supply Chain Security & SBOMs. What invariants, failure modes, and observability do you require?
interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Start from invariants, choose the pattern that preserves them, and add metrics for the known failure modes.
commonPitfalls: Optimizing throughput before defining correctness boundaries.

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: A Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) is a machine-readable inventory (SPDX or CycloneDX) of every direct and transitive package, OS layer, and binary inside a build artifact. Paired with cryptographic attestations (Cosign/Sigstore) and VEX advisories, it lets teams answer 'Are we exposed to CVE-X?' in seconds rather than days.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: Dependency-Track applies the primary invariant and coordinates with Kubernetes Admission.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, Kubernetes Admission experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Bind SBOM generation to the immutable OCI image digest (`sha256:...`) inside the final release job and reject images without matching digest attestations.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Generate CycloneDX or SPDX SBOMs inside your CI build, sign them with Sigstore Cosign alongside the container digest, and filter noise with VEX before blocking deploys.
Avoid trap: Generating an SBOM from `requirements.txt` without pinned hashes (`pip freeze`) or lockfiles, missing transitive dependency versions.
Avoid trap: Storing SBOM JSONs as ephemeral CI build logs instead of attaching them to OCI registries or ingesting them into Dependency-Track/Guac.
When to reach for it: Containerized and cloud-native services shipping to production where fast blast-radius queries across hundreds of microservices are critical.
When to reach for it: Enterprise B2B software, FedRAMP, or US Executive Order 14028 compliance where customers demand verifiable SPDX/CycloneDX manifests per release.

putItTogether.title: Putting Supply Chain Sbom Together
putItTogether.summary: Generate CycloneDX or SPDX SBOMs inside your CI build, sign them with Sigstore Cosign alongside the container digest, and filter noise with VEX before blocking deploys.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Supply Chain Sbom before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: Querying `pkg:maven/org.apache.commons/commons-text@1.9` in OWASP Dependency-Track returns the exact 11 affected image digests and owning teams in 90 seconds, rather than running 140 CI rebuilds.
